subject: Migration PoC: Architecture review & technical deep-dive — scheduling
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Bob Williams <bob.williams@acme-corp.com>
Date: Fri, 1 May 2026 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Migration PoC — architecture review request and scheduling

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our engineering leadership is interested in a deeper architecture review before we kick off a formal PoC — specifically to understand how Redwood would fit into our existing infra (k8s + custom quantized models) and what the migration path looks like from our current inference provider and self-hosted stack.

Can we schedule a technical deep-dive next week (45–60 minutes)? Prefer afternoons PT. Key goals for the session:
- High-level architecture and integration points (networking, auth, data flow)
- Model compatibility and quantization concerns
- PoC success criteria and test dataset/traffic patterns
- Timeline and environment provisioning needs

I've attached our current architecture diagram and a short list of questions to help guide the conversation.

Proposed times (PT):
- Tue 2026-05-05 1:00pm–2:00pm
- Wed 2026-05-06 3:00pm–4:00pm

If those don't work, happy to take whatever your team can offer.

Best,
Alice Chen
Senior Engineering Manager
Acme Corp

Attachments: acme_current_architecture_20260501.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 May 2026 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Migration PoC — architecture review request and scheduling

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the clear scope. We'd love to run that deep-dive. Dev (solutions engineer) and Ethan (runtime architect) are copied — they'll cover integration and performance/quantization questions respectively.

We can do either of your proposed slots except Tue 1pm PT is a conflict for Ethan. Suggested alternatives (PT):
- Tue 2026-05-05 3:00pm–4:00pm
- Thu 2026-05-07 2:00pm–3:00pm

Agenda (proposed, 60m):
1) 5m intros & current state recap
2) 20m Redwood architecture & recommended integration patterns
3) 15m Q&A on model compatibility / quantization / KV cache concerns
4) 10m PoC scope, success criteria, and timeline
5) 10m next steps / provisioning checklist

Pre-reads attached: Redwood PoC checklist and a short PoC requirements template — if you can drop a test dataset link and any topology constraints (VPC peering, inbound access controls) before the meeting, we'll prepare a proposed PoC plan.

If you prefer a shorter 45m session, we can trim the PoC timeline discussion and follow up with a dedicated call for that.

Possible meeting host: myself. We can provide a demo environment within 3–5 business days after the PoC kickoff.

I can send a calendar invite once we lock a time.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_poc_checklist.xlsx, poc_requirements_template.pdf
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme-corp.com>

Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Migration PoC — architecture review request and scheduling

Marissa — thanks for the quick reply and for looping Dev and Ethan.

Apologies, we just had a calendar change on our end. The Tue 3pm PT slot is actually still tight — would Thu 2026-05-07 11:00am–12:00pm ET (8:00am–9:00am PT) work for your team? If not, we can do Tue 2026-05-05 10:00am–11:00am PT (limited availability).

A few notes so you can prep:
- We run inference on a mix of k8s (self-hosted) and an older managed provider; the PoC should validate both routing and fallbacks.
- Our models are often quantized to int8 with custom kernels; Ethan might want to see a sample artifact format — happy to share after we confirm NDA/POC scope.
- Data residency requirement: testing and logs must stay in us-east1 for the PoC.

I'll upload a short topology diagram to the linked folder as well. Prefer a slightly earlier meeting if possible.

Best,
Alice
